title: Project Repository Structure and Maintainable Layout
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and value of Project Repository Structure and Maintainable Layout.
Apply project repository structure and maintainable layout to a Python project scenario.
Identify decisions and trade-offs relevant to project repository structure and maintainable layout.
Review common mistakes and risks in project repository structure and maintainable layout.
Produce a verifiable project artifact using project repository structure and maintainable layout principles.

understand.concept: A repository layout organizes source code, tests, documentation, configuration and build metadata. A clear structure separates application packages from generated files and local environments. The src layout can help tests exercise the installed package.
understand.whyItMatters: A predictable repository reduces onboarding friction and accidental coupling.
understand.analogy: A labelled filing system separates original records, working copies and instructions.
understand.analogyLimit: There is no single layout for every project; structure should match project size and packaging needs.
understand.summary: Project Repository Structure and Maintainable Layout helps learners plan and deliver maintainable Python projects.

explain.narrative: Keep importable code in a package, tests in a dedicated location and usage notes in documentation. Exclude virtual environments, caches, secrets and generated output from version control. Add a README with setup and test commands.

examples.title: Generated folders
examples.explanation: Generated environments should not be committed.

examples.title: Test command
examples.explanation: Reproducible commands help contributors verify the project.

practise.guidedTask: Design a repository tree for a CLI task manager.
practise.independentTask: Restructure a flat project into domain, adapters, CLI and tests.
hints: Separate source from tests and documentation.
Keep secrets and virtual environments out of version control.
Add project metadata and a setup guide.
Avoid excessive folders for a tiny project.
Test the installed package when packaging matters.
practise.challenge: Propose a structure for a finance tracker and explain each directory.
validationCriteria: The project concept is accurately explained and applied.
All examples execute with documented output on Python 3.13.
The proposed artifact is testable and appropriate to stated requirements.

questions.prompt: What is a common purpose of a tests directory?
questions.answer: Keep automated tests separate from application implementation
options: Keep automated tests separate from application implementation

questions.prompt: Why exclude virtual environments from version control?
questions.explanation: Environments are reproducible from dependency metadata.

questions.prompt: What does a README commonly provide?

options: Project purpose, setup, usage and test instructions
questions.explanation: It is a starting point for readers.

questions.prompt: What is one benefit of a src layout?
questions.answer: It helps tests avoid accidental imports from the repository root
options: It helps tests avoid accidental imports from the repository root
